comments.value:
For instance, a crescent rose weapon (ruby's scythe from rwby) that transforms
but as it is you  have to put a bunch of parameters on your avatar, new layers on your FX, and synced parameters in your parameters file
When it could just have it's own animator that handles all that.
and instead "put this ball on your back, put this ball on your right hand. Make a new "submenu" on your menu, put this item into it - you're done."
the vrchat discord channels are flooded with people who want to add animated stuff to their avatar, even parent constraints, and don't know how. Every day people have to explain this  stuff, when it could be SO much easier if the objects people sell on booth (and eventually on vrchat) had their own self-contained way of doing this and all you needed was to add a menu item, and then 2-3 parent constraint source gameobjects

details:
I was making a weapon to give a friend, and I tried to put everything on an animator on the weapon to make it work.. but found there was no way to actually make said animator receive any parameters that were triggered. In this case I was grabbing a bone on the weapon's armature, to get the Switch_IsGrabbed bool to say true. The behavior I was hoping for was that the weapon's animator would see that parameter change, and thus run the sequence of animations on itself, but instead what I got was it ignoring the parameter, even though it was in both my personal animator, parameters file, and it's own animator parameter and thus doing nothing at all. 
Adding this would make it much easier for people who make attachments and weapons for avatars to make them packages that could easily be given without the need to clutter a player's own FX layer with extra layers. All you would need to do is add the instructions "add this parameter(bool) to your FX layer and Parameters file" and then all the work would be done inside the attachment/weapon/clothing. 

if it's not affecting my personal avatar in any way
why do the parameters need to be on my avatar? Why do the animation layers need to be on my avatar, and not on the attachment with it's own animations, armature, and textures? 
the attachment is the only thing that needs them, so it can say "hey this parameter of mine was toggled, so let's do this"
 if the weapons own animator worked like that then the whole system of doing a parent constraint could be in-weapon too
"put this ball on your right hand, put this ball on your left, but this ball on your back or hip"

animator inside says "player grabbed the barrel with left hand(physbone_isgrabbed) , switch parent constraints and aim constraint to two-handed mode"

inside the gun's animator would also be a layer that says "if gestureright = fist, shoot" , as you (the creator) would put GestureRight, GestureLeft on it's layer parameters


this would also remove the need for things like VRlabs avatars 3.0 manager that merge FX and Parameters because they would be self-contained on the weapon/attachment/clothing

I don't think this would be -too- hard to accomplish, it seems like something rather trivial to set in the SDK since avatars 3.0 and unity in general can do so many things. 
This also helps your idea of a future "player market" because it makes things that are easier to sell to a player. 
Even moreso if you make it so that the parameters can be triggered without having to be added to the player's own FX, meaning all they have to do is add the attachment/weapon/clothing in unity, upload, and go.  
I hope you consider this post, as it would make the process of sharing or selling creations much easier
title: [Feature Request] Animators that receieve parameters for sub-meshes
